themes_detail.label: Food Poisoning Spike
themes_detail.summary: East Harlem is experiencing a 500% spike in food poisoning complaints THIS WEEK (3 complaints vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks), suggesting a potential foodborne illness outbreak or contamination event affecting multiple residents.
evidence: 3 food poisoning complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% increase, z-score: 5.0)
Represents the most acute health spike in the recent data window
Timing and clustering suggest possible common source (restaurant, food vendor, or event)
reporting_angles: Contact DOHMH to determine if complaints are linked to specific establishment or food source; interview affected residents
Check Department of Health inspection records for any recent violations or closure orders in the district

themes_detail.label: Encampment Surge
themes_detail.summary: Homelessness and street encampments in East Harlem surged 487% LAST WEEK (11 complaints vs. 1.9 weekly average), marking a dramatic acceleration in visible street homelessness and suggesting possible new camps near transit hubs or parks.
evidence: 11 encampment complaints last week vs. 1.9 weekly average (487% spike, z-score: 5.4)
Sustained pattern: Safety complaints also up 246% three weeks ago (16 complaints vs. 4.6 avg), suggesting ongoing destabilization
No recent Reddit or CB discussion yet—suggests story is breaking
reporting_angles: Map encampments by location (parks, subway entrances, residential blocks); interview street outreach teams and residents about triggers for surge
Cross-reference with city shelter placement data to determine if encampment surge correlates with intake freezes or bed shortage

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints in East Harlem jumped 250% LAST WEEK (91 complaints vs. 26 weekly average), the largest noise spike in the dataset and suggesting a new persistent source (construction, venue, transit disruption) affecting outdoor spaces.
evidence: 91 street/sidewalk noise complaints last week vs. 26 weekly average (250% increase, z-score: 3.44)
Distinct from residential noise (445 complaints over 90 days), suggesting outdoor/public-realm source
Aligns with district's standing budget request for additional traffic enforcement—suggests chronic traffic/street noise problem now worsening
reporting_angles: Identify location clusters of noise complaints (via 311 map); contact NYPD and DOT to ask about recent events, construction permits, or transit changes
Interview residents on high-complaint blocks about specific noise sources (trucks, bars, street vendors, subway work)

themes_detail.label: Dead Animal & Litter Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Sanitation failures in East Harlem are accelerating: Litter basket requests exploded 2300% LAST WEEK (3 vs. 0.1 average) and dead animal complaints surged 1500% (4 vs. 0.2 average), both z-score 8.6+, suggesting acute public health and cleanliness breakdown.
evidence: Litter basket requests: 3 last week vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
Dead animal complaints: 4 last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (1500% spike, z-score: 8.66)
Animal in park complaints also up 357% (4 vs. 0.9 avg), suggesting wildlife pressure driven by garbage/filth
Converges with district's standing budget request for graffiti removal and cleaning—chronic issue now acute
reporting_angles: Contact Sanitation Department to ask why litter basket maintenance and dead animal removal have deteriorated; check for staffing or service cuts
Photograph and report on conditions in parks and high-complaint blocks; interview residents on rodent/pest sightings

themes_detail.label: Root & Sewer Infrastructure Failures
themes_detail.summary: Root and sewer damage complaints in East Harlem spiked 380% THREE WEEKS AGO (3 vs. 0.6 weekly average, z-score: 3.41), suggesting aging subsurface infrastructure failure that may presage flooding, water outages, or backups during heavy rain.
evidence: Root/sewer/sidewalk complaints: 3 filed 3 weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly average (380% spike, z-score: 3.41)
Aligns with district's standing budget request for DEP capital improvements—suggests known chronic problem surfacing acutely
Timing suggests this may have stabilized or been repair-addressed; recommend verification of current status
reporting_angles: Contact DEP to ask about aging sewer lines in East Harlem and any emergency repairs or failures in past 3 weeks
Check for any water main breaks or service advisories issued in the district; interview affected residents about sewer backups or flooding
